title: Cheaper than that one
title_target: Πιο φθηνό από αυτό — Pyoh fthee-noh ah-poh ahf-toh
goal: Compare two things and name the most — in two equally correct ways, plus six comparison words that break the pattern.
bekal: say "the most" with ο πιο and ο καλύτερος
say two things are equal with τόσο … όσο

dialogs.title: ΔΙΑΛΟΓΟΣ — Looking for a souvenir
dialogs.intro: Ana is looking for a present for her sister in a small shop in Monastiraki. Notice that the seller uses two different ways of comparing in one sentence — and both are right.

notes: **There are two ways to compare, and both are equally correct.** The first puts **πιο** before the adjective: *πιο ακριβή*, *πιο μεγάλος*, *πιο φθηνό*. The second uses the ending **-τερος**: *ακριβότερη*, *μεγαλύτερος*, *φθηνότερο*. ⚠️ The first is heard more and is easier to form; the second is more common in writing. Use πιο when in doubt — it's never wrong. (Like English "more expensive" vs. "cheaper".)

**"Than" is από**, and the word after it takes the object form, as after every preposition: *πιο ακριβή από **την** άλλη*, *πιο μεγάλος από **τον** αδερφό μου*. ⚠️ Some speakers also use **παρά** for this, but από is far more common.

**Comparatives still agree in gender with the noun**, just like ordinary adjectives: πιο μεγάλ**ος** δρόμος, πιο μεγάλ**η** πόλη, πιο μεγάλ**ο** σπίτι. The -τερος form too: μεγαλύτερ**ος**, μεγαλύτερ**η**, μεγαλύτερ**ο**.

**For "the most", put an article before the comparative.** *η πιο ελαφριά* (the lightest), *το καλύτερο δώρο* (the best present), *ο πιο μεγάλος* (the biggest). Add **από όλους / όλες / όλα** for emphasis: *από όλες* = of all.

⚠️ **Six comparatives break the pattern** — and all are common: καλός → **καλύτερος** (better), κακός → **χειρότερος** (worse), μεγάλος → **μεγαλύτερος**, μικρός → **μικρότερος**, πολύ → **περισσότερο** (more), λίγο → **λιγότερο** (less). These six must be learned as they are; the rest are regular.
**Πολύ πιο = "much more".** *Πολύ πιο φθηνό* — much cheaper. *Λίγο πιο ακριβό* — a bit more expensive. These two boosters make your comparisons sound far more alive.
**Μεγαλύτερος and μικρότερος also mean "older" and "younger"** for siblings — just as English says "big brother" and "little sister": *ο μεγαλύτερος αδερφός μου* = my older brother.

**Θέλετε να το τυλίξω;** — "shall I wrap it?". Note the **το** before the verb: object pronouns stand **before** the verb, not after it. *Το ξέρω* (I know it), *Σε βλέπω* (I see you), *Τον ρωτάω* (I ask him). ⚠️ This is the reverse of English and takes time to get used to.

grammars.title: Two ways to compare
body: Compare the two columns. The meanings are identical; only the tone and usage habits differ.
after: **The full pattern:** *Η Αθήνα είναι **πιο μεγάλη από** τη Θεσσαλονίκη.* — Athens is bigger than Thessaloniki. Or: *Η Αθήνα είναι **μεγαλύτερη από** τη Θεσσαλονίκη.*
⚠️ For adverbs (not adjectives), the form ends in -α: *Τρέχει **πιο γρήγορα**.* — He runs faster. *Μιλάει **καλύτερα** από μένα.* — She speaks better than me.

grammars.title: The most, and the same
body: The top degree is formed just by adding an article. No new forms to learn.
after: **Ο καλύτερος** on its own means "the best": *Είσαι ο καλύτερος!* — You're the best! A very common compliment.
⚠️ **Χειρότερος** ("worse") is used far more than *πιο κακός*, which sounds like you're talking about wicked character, not quality.

blocks.title: Ready-made sentences for the shop
items: **Ψάχνω ένα δώρο / μια μπλούζα.** — I'm looking for a present / a T-shirt.
**Μπορώ να το δοκιμάσω;** — Can I try it on? · **Έχετε μεγαλύτερο μέγεθος;** — Do you have a bigger size?
**Έχετε άλλο χρώμα;** — Do you have another color? · **Έχει έκπτωση;** — Is there a discount?

**Είναι λίγο ακριβό για μένα.** — It's a bit expensive for me. ⚠️ In ordinary shops bargaining isn't usual; at the Monastiraki flea market and in small souvenir shops this sentence sometimes brings the price down a little.
**Θα το σκεφτώ.** — I'll think about it. The politest way to leave without buying.
**Θέλετε να το τυλίξω;** — Shall I wrap it? Answer: *Ναι, είναι δώρο.* — Yes, it's a present.
